(a) In General.—Subparagraph (D) of section 1400L(d)(2) is amended by striking “January 1, 2012” and inserting “January 1, 2014”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to bonds issued after December 31, 2011.

fable.w: This section only extends a date in a tax provision governing bonds and sets an effective date. There is no tempting reading: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: The amendment made by this section shall apply to bonds issued after December 31, 2011.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment that changes a specific date in another statute and defines the effective date for that change. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely legislative housekeeping.
qwen_block.s:
(a) In General.—Subparagraph (D) of section 1400L(d)(2) is amended by striking “January 1, 2012” and inserting “January 1, 2014”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to bonds issued after December 31, 2011.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment: it replaces the date "January 1, 2012" with "January 1, 2014" and applies the change to bonds issued after December 31, 2011. No one outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any federal decision, and nothing here requires a hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. Mentioning bonds does not create a process that brings outside parties into a decision.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting wrong reading:** The word "bonds" might suggest issuers or investors outside the government taking part in something. That reading fails. The section only moves a date in a tax provision (section 1400L(d)(2)(D)) and sets an effective date. No outside party is consulted, there is no hearing, comment period or rulemaking, and no one gains a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends a specific date in a statute and defines the effective date of that amendment. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with outside parties. The text is purely procedural regarding the statute's timeline and does not involve any external participation in a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s:
(a) In General.—Subparagraph (D) of section 1400L(d)(2) is amended by striking “January 1, 2012” and inserting “January 1, 2014”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to bonds issued after December 31, 2011.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the effective date of a bond program affects the public or entities applying for bonds, thus implying participation. However, the text itself only describes a legislative amendment to a date and its applicability. It does not establish any process for consulting with, hearing from, or coordinating with outside parties. The definition requires an active mechanism of participation (like a hearing, comment period, or advisory board), which is absent here.
